entities.summary: Kent Alan Hrbek, nicknamed "Herbie", is an American former Major League Baseball first baseman. He played his entire 14-year baseball career with the Minnesota Twins (1981–1994). Hrbek batted left-handed and threw right-handed. He hit the first home run in the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome on April 3, 1982, in an exhibition game against the Phillies. Fans knew Hrbek as an outstanding defensive player, perennial slugger, and charismatic hometown favorite. Former Twins pitcher Jim Kaat considered Hrbek to be the best defensive first baseman he had ever seen, despite him never winning a Gold Glove at the position.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a perennial slugger and charismatic hometown favorite, Kent Hrbek's outstanding defensive play and impressive home run totals helped shape the Minnesota Twins' success in the late 1980s and early 1990s, contributing to their World Series championships in 1987 and 1991.
